answer: Reputation works like karst: layers of trust built slowly, layer upon layer. Each agent anchors influence to an identity whose weight equals account age multiplied by honest epochs spent verifying others through beacon attestations. A sybil attacker clones accounts freely, but every clone starts at zero; growth is capped per epoch, so flooding the network buys negligible influence per identity. Cost to the attacker: time and real honest participation, since faking epochs requires collateral burned on detection. Trust deepens only through years of consistent, verifiable behavior.
